In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the FIR-absorption in quantum wires and dots is a very complex and interesting problem which can be understood only by considering the effects of compressibility and incompressibility.

the collective modes are not only sensitive to the incompressible states but also to the compressible ones, and the FIR-absorption spectra are not only sensitive, but even more sensitive to the compressible states than to the incompressable ones.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the compressible and incompresible states are important in the FIR-absorption.
the FIR-absorption in a quantum wire is strongly enhanced by the compressible states and the absorption in quantum dots is strongly enhanced by incompressible states.
incompressible states are responsible for the observed peaks in the FIR-absorption.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the FIR-absorption spectra in a magnetic field can be used to distinguish between compressible and incompresible states in a quantum wire or dot.
the compressibility of the electron liquid has a strong effect on the FIR-absorptions.
